citations.quote: Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\operatorname{int}(D)\cap F=\varnothing$ and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha=D\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\beta=D\cap\partial M$, and $\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\cup\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

An essential smooth embedded circle in the standard torus $T=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ represents a nonzero primitive integral homology class. A finite disjoint family of essential smooth circles can be carried by a jointly smooth ambient isotopy of $T$ to parallel affine circles. Two essential circles with the same primitive unoriented class are smoothly ambient isotopic. The components between disjoint essential circles have smooth annulus parameters, with prescribed product collars on their boundary circles. No choice axiom is assumed.

Likewise two smooth spanning arcs of a parametrized annulus with the same endpoints and relative winding number are smoothly ambient isotopic relative to any collars on which they already agree. When disjoint, they have a smooth disk-strip parameter; disjoint essential circles in a parametrized annulus have smooth annulus-strip parameters. All isotopies may be stationary near their time endpoints.

For $n=2,3$, a given smooth ball embedding $e:D^n\to N$ into a connected boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold is isotopic through embeddings to a small coordinate round ball, and that embedding isotopy extends ambiently with compact support. For a parametrized smooth $n$-ball $B$ and a parametrized smooth boundary $(n-1)$-disk $W$, the pair $(B,W)$ is diffeomorphic to the standard ball with a hemispherical window. The diffeomorphism can retain the specified window parameter, using stereographic parameters on the standard hemisphere and allowing the necessary orientation of that parameter. No choice axiom is assumed.

Consequently, attaching a parametrized smooth $n$-ball to a smooth $n$-manifold along such a window does not change its diffeomorphism type, provided an attaching collar and corner rounding are supplied. The resulting diffeomorphism is supported in the added ball and an arbitrarily small receiving collar. The inverse assertion holds for removing a ball that meets the boundary in exactly one such window with the supplied collar charts. In dimension two the windows are intervals.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth three-manifold, possibly nonorientable and with boundary, and let $f:F\to M$ be a smooth embedding of a compact smooth surface with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$. Transversality to $\partial M$ is not assumed. Given an open neighborhood $U$ of $C=f(\partial F)$, there is a jointly smooth map $(x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)$ such that each $f_t$ is an embedding, $f_0=f$, every $f_t$ agrees with $f$ on $\partial F$ and outside $f^{-1}(U)$, and $f_t$ is neatly proper for every $t>0$. Time may instead be reparametrized to be stationary near both endpoints; in that version neatness holds after the initial stationary interval.

There is also a jointly continuous ambient isotopy of homeomorphisms $H_t:M\to M$, starting at the identity, supported in $U$, fixing $\partial M$ pointwise, and satisfying $H_t f=f_t$. The construction makes $H_t$ jointly smooth on $(M\setminus C)\times[0,1]$. If $f$ is already neat, the same $f_t$ alternatively admits a jointly smooth ambient extension fixing $\partial M$. No smooth ambient extension at an original tangency is asserted.

Let $F_0=f(F)$ be a compact two-sided smoothly embedded surface in a compact smooth three-manifold, with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$, and let $F_1,H_1$ be its angular neatification from [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]]. The ambient manifold may be nonorientable. If $F_1$ has a smooth compressing disk or smooth boundary-compressing disk, then $F_0$ has a disk of the same type. Boundary-compressing disks can also be transported in the opposite direction: if $F_0$ has one, then $F_1$ has one. Consequently absence of either kind of smooth disk passes from $F_0$ to $F_1$.

Here the boundary-compressing witness has one boundary arc in the surface and the other in $\partial M$, its interior missing both. The construction allows the broader convention of ordinary smooth disk embeddings with tangential endpoint contact, and also gives smooth corner-disk witnesses with transverse surface arcs when that convention is used. No smooth ambient removal of an original surface tangency is asserted.

derivations.claim: First apply [F9] to the given surface, fixed pointwise on its boundary. The resulting surface is neat. Incompressibility passes to it, and a boundary-compressing witness passes in either direction; absence of boundary compressions therefore passes as well. Work with this neat representative for the following smooth collar constructions. The boundary-fixing topological ambient extension pulls any resulting boundary-parallel product back to the actual original surface. Thus this preparation does not add a neatness hypothesis to the Statement. Write $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha$ is the essential proper arc in $A$ and $\beta$ lies in a boundary torus $T$. In an annulus every essential proper arc joins its two boundary circles: cut along a radial spanning arc and use a lift to the strip; an arc returning to the same boundary cuts off a disk there. Consequently both boundary circles of $A$ lie on this same $T$. They are essential on $T$: otherwise choose an innermost disk bounded by one of them in $T$, push it inward off the annulus collar, and obtain a compression of $A$. By [F2] the two circles cut $T$ into two parametrized annuli. The interior of $\beta$ misses them and joins them, so it spans one of these annuli, denoted $A_0$.

Push the interior of $A_0$ a little into its inward collar, keeping its rim on $A$, and round the rim. The union $S=A\cup A_0$ is a torus with a displayed corner before rounding. The curve $\alpha\cup\beta$ on it meets a core of $A$ once algebraically, not merely modulo two: $\alpha$ is a spanning arc of the annulus. It is therefore a nonseparating essential circle. Compress $S$ along $D$, taking two parallel copies of $D$ in its disk neighborhood; the result is a sphere. Irreducibility supplies a parametrized ball bounded by it. The disk neighborhood lies outside this ball: its strip along $\beta$ is joined to $\partial M$ through the gap left when that strip was removed from $A_0$, without crossing the compressed sphere. A ball in the interior cannot contain that boundary collar. Restoring the disk neighborhood therefore attaches one marked $1$-handle to the ball, rather than removing a possibly knotted handle from it. Its two attaching disk windows have the actual parallel-copy parameters of $D$. They can be put in standard positions by [F3]: standardize one window, shrink the other in the connected complement of the first on the boundary sphere, and move it to the opposite standard disk by the finite supported construction in [F3]'s Proof 1.1–2.1, fixing the first. Thus the restored region $U$ is a smooth solid torus with meridian disk the cocore of this handle. Its boundary is the displayed $S$; all corner changes are restored by the original quadrant collars.

The marking is essential. In the product coordinates $U=D^2\times S^1$ supplied by that ball and handle, let $(\mu,\lambda)$ denote the meridian-longitude basis of its boundary. Each rim circle of $A$ meets the cocore boundary once algebraically, because it meets $\alpha\cup\beta$ once. Hence its slope is $p\mu+q\lambda$ with $q=\pm1$. By [F2] normalize the two rim circles to affine circles of that slope. The entire boundary isotopy extends into a radial annulus of $D^2\times S^1$: in the boundary radial coordinate use the same formula $(r,x)\mapsto(r,h_{\eta(r)t}(x))$ as [F3], identity near the inner solid torus. The product diffeomorphism $(z,e^{i\theta})\mapsto(e^{ip\theta}z,e^{iq\theta})$, with inverse $(z,e^{i\varphi})\mapsto(e^{-ipq\varphi}z,e^{iq\varphi})$, carries longitudinal circles to that slope, up to replacing $p$ by its negative according to the chosen inverse. Apply its inverse. The two complementary boundary annuli now correspond to the two arcs between two points on $\partial D^2$, times $S^1$. The disk with one of these marked arcs is a rectangle with its bottom edge marked, with the usual rounded-corner interpretation, by [F3] in dimension two. Taking its product with $S^1$ gives a product between the corresponding annuli: the first is $A\times\{0\}$, and $A\times\{1\}\cup\partial A\times[0,1]$ is the second annulus $A_0$. Restore the retained quadrant collars to get this product for the actual original $A$ and boundary annulus in $\partial M$. This proves boundary-parallelity in [F1]'s precise sense. The winding-one condition from $D$ is what justifies this product; complementary annuli in an arbitrary solid torus do not suffice. All selected charts, windows and curve moves were finite, and [F2]–[F3] require no choice.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Every orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $g:S^2\to S^2$ is joined to the identity by a jointly smooth isotopy of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, stationary near its time endpoints. Consequently every smooth diffeomorphism $b:\partial B_0\to\partial B_1$ between the boundaries of two parametrized smooth $3$-balls extends to a smooth diffeomorphism $B_0\to B_1$. In the radial boundary collars supplied by their parametrizations, the extension can be required to have the product form $(x,r)\mapsto(b(x),r)$ on one smaller collar. Its orientation agrees with the orientation of $b$ on the boundaries, using the outward-normal convention.

This asserts existence of an isotopy for each given map; it does not assert a deformation retraction parametrized by the entire diffeomorphism group.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The bounded region of a smooth embedded
circle in the oriented plane, together with its boundary, is a smooth manifold
with boundary diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Let $D_0,D_1$ be two
such closed regions. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary
diffeomorphism $b:\partial D_0\to\partial D_1$ extends to an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $B:D_0\to D_1$. More precisely, for
specified smooth inward collars $c_i:\partial D_i\times[0,\epsilon)\to D_i$
with $c_i(p,0)=p$, the extension may be required to satisfy
$B(c_0(p,r))=c_1(b(p),r)$ for every sufficiently small $r\ge0$. In addition, given interior points $p_i\in D_i$ and an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $q$ from a neighborhood of $p_0$ onto a neighborhood of $p_1$, the extension can agree with $q$ near $p_0$ while retaining the prescribed boundary collars.

All isotopies below are jointly smooth diffeotopies, stationary near the time endpoints.

1. On $A=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\times[0,1]$, every smooth diffeomorphism fixing both boundary circles pointwise is isotopic relative to the boundary to exactly one twist
$$D_k(\theta,u)=(\theta+k\rho(u),u),\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,$$
where $\rho$ is a fixed smooth function equal to zero near $0$ and one near $1$. If the map initially fixes a boundary collar, a common smaller collar can be fixed throughout this isotopy. Without fixing the boundary, every annulus diffeomorphism is isotopic to one of the four maps $(\theta,u)\mapsto(\varepsilon\theta,u)$ or $(\theta,u)\mapsto(\varepsilon\theta,1-u)$, with $\varepsilon=\pm1$.
2. Every smooth diffeomorphism of $T^2=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ inducing the identity on $H_1(T^2;\mathbb Z)$ is smoothly isotopic to the identity. Consequently every torus diffeomorphism is smoothly isotopic to the linear torus map inducing its integral unimodular matrix on $H_1$.

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact orientable smooth three-manifold and let $\mathcal A$ be a finite disjoint family of properly embedded two-sided annuli. Suppose each map $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(M)$ is injective and every component of the cut-open manifold $M\mathbin{\|}\mathcal A$, with its boundary corners rounded, is irreducible. Then $M$ is irreducible. The family may be empty, and its annuli need not be separating or boundary-incompressible.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F$ be a compact smooth surface with boundary, let $M$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$ be a closed embedded smooth surface. If $i:F\to M$ is a smooth embedding whose boundary restriction $i|_{\partial F}$ is transverse to $S$, then there is a smooth isotopy $i_t:F\to M$ through embeddings, fixed on a neighbourhood of $\partial F$, such that $i_1(F)$ is transverse to $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold, let $F$ be a compact connected smooth subsurface of $\partial M$, and let $N\lhd\pi_1(F)$ be normal. If a continuous disk map into $M$ has its boundary in $\operatorname{Int}F$ with class outside $N$, there is a smoothly properly embedded disk in $M$ whose boundary lies in $\operatorname{Int}F$ and has class outside $N$. No pointwise preservation of the original boundary loop is asserted.

Consequently a compact neatly properly embedded two-sided smooth surface $S$ in such a compact orientable smooth three-manifold is incompressible if and only if its inclusion induces an injection on fundamental groups, component by component. Here incompressibility means absence of a smooth embedded compressing disk, with the conventions of the indicated definition.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth three-manifold, possibly nonorientable and with boundary, and let $f:F\to M$ be a smooth embedding of a compact smooth surface with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$. Transversality to $\partial M$ is not assumed. Given an open neighborhood $U$ of $C=f(\partial F)$, there is a jointly smooth map $(x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)$ such that each $f_t$ is an embedding, $f_0=f$, every $f_t$ agrees with $f$ on $\partial F$ and outside $f^{-1}(U)$, and $f_t$ is neatly proper for every $t>0$. Time may instead be reparametrized to be stationary near both endpoints; in that version neatness holds after the initial stationary interval.

There is also a jointly continuous ambient isotopy of homeomorphisms $H_t:M\to M$, starting at the identity, supported in $U$, fixing $\partial M$ pointwise, and satisfying $H_t f=f_t$. The construction makes $H_t$ jointly smooth on $(M\setminus C)\times[0,1]$. If $f$ is already neat, the same $f_t$ alternatively admits a jointly smooth ambient extension fixing $\partial M$. No smooth ambient extension at an original tangency is asserted.

Let $F_0=f(F)$ be a compact two-sided smoothly embedded surface in a compact smooth three-manifold, with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$, and let $F_1,H_1$ be its angular neatification from [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]]. The ambient manifold may be nonorientable. If $F_1$ has a smooth compressing disk or smooth boundary-compressing disk, then $F_0$ has a disk of the same type. Boundary-compressing disks can also be transported in the opposite direction: if $F_0$ has one, then $F_1$ has one. Consequently absence of either kind of smooth disk passes from $F_0$ to $F_1$.

Here the boundary-compressing witness has one boundary arc in the surface and the other in $\partial M$, its interior missing both. The construction allows the broader convention of ordinary smooth disk embeddings with tangential endpoint contact, and also gives smooth corner-disk witnesses with transverse surface arcs when that convention is used. No smooth ambient removal of an original surface tangency is asserted.

Assume full AC. Every compact topological three-manifold $M$, with boundary allowed, is homeomorphic to the realization of a finite combinatorial three-manifold triangulation, with boundary allowed (the empty complex when $M=\varnothing$). Its boundary is the realization of a subcomplex. Thus $M$ admits a finite compatible PL structure, without any previously supplied smooth or PL structure on its interior.

If a TOP product collar of the boundary, together with a finite PL structure on its boundary surface, has already been supplied, the new PL structure may be chosen equal to that product PL structure on a smaller boundary neighborhood. No smooth marking or smooth ambient isotopy is asserted. Full AC remains the hypothesis of this theorem; no choice-free theorem is obtained by omitting that premise.

Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable piecewise linear three-manifold with a given finite compatible manifold triangulation and with boundary a subcomplex. Let $F\subset\partial M$ be a connected compact piecewise linear subsurface and $N\trianglelefteq\pi_1(F)$ a normal subgroup. Suppose there is a continuous map $f:(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(M,F)$ whose boundary lies in the relative interior of $F$ and has class outside $N$. Then there is a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$, with boundary in the relative interior of $F$, whose boundary class is outside $N$.

In particular, if a connected boundary component has noninjective induced fundamental-group map into $M$, it contains an essential simple closed curve bounding a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$. Boundary classes outside $N$ are understood up to conjugation by a basepath in $F$.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

Every element of $G\ast_KH$ has a unique normal form $s_1\cdots s_nk$ relative to fixed transversals. A normal word of positive length is nonidentity. The represented group and these conclusions are independent of the chosen transversals.

Fix an HNN extension in associated-subgroup notation and choose transversal data
$(S_-,S_+)$ as in [[def-choice-of-transversals-for-hnn-normal-forms]]. Then
every element of the HNN extension is represented by a unique transversal normal
form

$$a_0t^{\varepsilon_1}a_1\cdots t^{\varepsilon_n}a_n.$$

In particular, the identity has the unique normal form with $n=0$ and
$a_0=e_A$.

$\operatorname{Deg}:\pi_1(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z,[0])\to(\mathbb Z,+)$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is

$$n\longmapsto[\omega_n].$$

For pointed topological spaces $(X,x_0)$ and $(Y,y_0)$, the coordinate projections induce a natural group isomorphism

$$\Theta:\pi_1(X\times Y,(x_0,y_0))\longrightarrow\pi_1(X,x_0)\times\pi_1(Y,y_0),\qquad [\gamma]\longmapsto([\pi_X\gamma],[\pi_Y\gamma]).$$

Its inverse sends $([\alpha],[\beta])$ to the class of the paired loop $s\mapsto(\alpha(s),\beta(s))$.

derivations.claim: The solid torus is irreducible. Embed it as a standard unknotted solid torus in $S^3$. A sphere in its interior has two ball sides by [F2]. Its exterior solid torus is connected and misses the sphere, so lies entirely on one side; the other ball is contained in $V$. We will use the following disk-push consequence with its smooth interpretation. If two smooth disks meet just along their common boundary and bound such a ball, their faces admit a common-boundary disk sweep through the ball. To retain the actual faces, take a thin rim collar first. At a transverse rim its normal section is a quadrant; at a previously shared collar first separate the two faces by a small normal graph. Parametrize the two faces by smooth disks with their prescribed rim collars, using [F3]. Round and truncate the rim; the remaining boundary is a smooth sphere with these marked disk and collar portions. The two disk maps and the intervening product annulus give a smooth boundary diffeomorphism to the corresponding standard rounded lens; [F3] extends it over the ball. Restore the quadrant rim using those same product collars. This gives a lens parameter retaining both faces and their rim coordinates. In this parameter use [F4]'s spherical-cap sweep; in the rim section its inward tangent runs between the two face tangents and stays nonzero. The sweep is jointly smooth, including at the disk center, by [F4]'s displayed formulas. It can be continued just past either face in its normal collar and extended ambiently by [F5]. If another surface misses the ball except in one face, the push removes that face's intersections and creates none. The support can be restricted to the ball and arbitrarily thin face and rim collars.

For the classification first replace $F$ by its neat representative using [F9]; both disk-obstruction hypotheses pass to it. Its boundary and abstract surface are unchanged. The topological ambient extension pulls a boundary-parallel product back to the original surface, and no smooth product at an original tangency is asserted. In the rest of the classification denote this neat representative again by $F$. The surface $F$ is compact, since its inclusion is proper and $V$ is compact, and it is orientable, since it is two-sided in oriented $V$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\operatorname{int}(D)\cap F=\varnothing$ and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha=D\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\beta=D\cap\partial M$, and $\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\cup\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible smooth three-manifold with a supplied finite whole-star smooth manifold triangulation $T$. Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite disjoint family of incompressible smooth tori in its interior. There is a jointly smooth ambient isotopy, fixed near $\partial M$ and stationary near its time endpoints, after which the family misses the vertices, crosses edges transversely in finitely many points, meets every triangular face in finitely many disjoint arcs joining different edges, and meets each tetrahedron in finitely many proper disks whose boundary crosses each of its edges at most once. The boundary patterns are therefore the four triangle and three quadrilateral patterns. The finitely many balls cut out inside each tetrahedron by those disks have supplied ball parameters retaining their disk faces and face-cell corners. All tori are moved simultaneously; the family may be empty.

These are smooth surfaces in a specified compatible triangulation. No identification of an arbitrary topological marking with a smooth or PL structure is asserted.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth three-manifold with a supplied finite whole-star smooth manifold triangulation. Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite disjoint two-sided closed smooth torus family in its interior, in normal disk position: each tetrahedron meets it in proper disks with the triangle or quadrilateral boundary patterns. Suppose all balls obtained by cutting individual tetrahedra along those disks have supplied ball parameters, with their disk faces and face-cell corners retained. Supply parameters of the rectangle face cells, taking their opposite edges on $\mathcal S$ as horizontal and their other two edges on triangulation edges as vertical.

Let $C$ be a connected component of $M$ cut open along $\mathcal S$ which meets every triangular face only in rectangle cells. Then $C$ is disjoint from $\partial M$ and is a topological interval bundle over a compact connected surface without boundary. Its bundle admits a locally flat embedded core surface $Q$, obtained as a section, and the base has a finite cellulation. If $C$ is not homeomorphic to $T^2\times I$, the core is one-sided and $C\setminus Q$ is connected. No choice axiom is assumed.

The conclusion is a topological interval-bundle parameterization from the specified finite data. It asserts neither smoothness nor compatibility with an unrelated marking.

Let $N$ be a connected Hausdorff topological three-manifold without boundary. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ be finitely many disjoint compact connected locally flat embedded surfaces without boundary. They may be one-sided and nonorientable. If $N\setminus\bigcup_j S_j$ is connected, their canonical mod-two fundamental classes have linearly independent images in $H_2(N;\mathbb F_2)$. The manifold may be noncompact and nonorientable, and the family may be empty. No choice axiom or ambient triangulation is assumed.

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible smooth three-manifold with nonempty boundary, and supply a finite compatible whole-star smooth manifold triangulation with $t$ triangular faces. Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite disjoint family of two-sided incompressible smooth interior tori. If no component of $M$ cut open along $\mathcal S$ is homeomorphic to $T^2\times I$, then
$$
|\mathcal S|\le 4t+\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M;\mathbb F_2)-1.
$$
Thus any process accumulating cuts whose every finite stage has this no-product property can make only finitely many cuts. The family may be empty.

The supplied triangulation is compatible with the smooth structure in the stated whole-star sense. This result asserts no compatibility of an arbitrary topological marking and does not alter the scope of any other finiteness item.

For every simplicial complex $K$ and abelian group $G$, there is a canonical
natural isomorphism $H_n^{\mathrm{simp}}(K;G)\cong H_n(|K|;G)$ for all $n$.
When the vertex set has a supplied total order, it is induced by the
simplicial-to-singular chain map of [[def-simplicial-to-singular-chain-map]],
extended $G$-linearly. Different supplied orders induce the same homology map.
For an arbitrary vertex set, the isomorphism is defined compatibly on its
finite subcomplexes and requires no choice principle.

derivations.claim: Apply [F2] to the given finite torus family for the very triangulation in the Statement. Its smooth ambient isotopy retains incompressibility, all cut-component homeomorphism types and the no-product condition. It puts the family into actual normal disks in each parametrized tetrahedron and disjoint arcs in each triangular face, joining distinct edges. This invokes the accepted marked normal-position construction rather than treating a surgery that changes a torus as an isotopy.

In each triangular face group the arcs by the pair of distinct edges they join. Within each of the three types they occur in a parallel stack. Between consecutive arcs of a stack is a rectangle, and collapsing those strips leaves at most one arc of each type, hence at most four complementary regions. Every nonrectangular region survives distinctly in this collapsed picture, so there are at most $4t$ such regions over all faces. The successive finite face-disk cuts and the marked rectangle product maps are supplied by [F2] and [F5]; no unparametrized polygon or missing side matching is being assumed.

Let $m$ be the number of cut components meeting all faces only in rectangles. By [F3] each is an interval bundle. The torus-product possibility is excluded by hypothesis. Thus they have disjoint one-sided compact locally flat cores $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$, and removing each core leaves its component connected. No ambient triangulation or smoothness of these cores is required.

Form the connected finite dual graph of all torus cuts, allowing loops, and choose a spanning tree. Let $k$ be the number of edges outside that tree. The corresponding $k$ tori, together with all the $Q_j$, have connected complement: remove the cores in the fully cut pieces, which remain connected by step2.1, and glue back the tree faces. A tree joins all the pieces and cannot create a new disconnection. Pass to $\operatorname{Int}M$ by the finite inward collar push in [F5], chosen disjoint from these compact surfaces; its homotopy fixes them and proves that the interior inclusion induces a homology isomorphism, while their complement remains connected. Now [F4] gives $k+m$ independent mod-two classes, so $k+m\le\beta$, where $\beta=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M;\mathbb F_2)$. This number is finite because the supplied triangulation is finite and its simplicial homology computes singular homology.

Write $n=|\mathcal T|$ and let $v$ be the number of cut components. The dual graph has $n$ edges, $v$ vertices and $k=n-v+1$ non-tree edges; thus $v=n-k+1$. Each component other than the $m$ rectangular-only ones contains a nonrectangular face region. A physical region belongs to just one cut component: its two tetrahedral sides are glued through its interior, or it is a boundary face with only one incident side. Distinct components therefore use distinct such regions, and step1.2 gives $v\le m+4t$.

Combining these inequalities yields $n+1\le k+m+4t\le\beta+4t$, which is exactly the stated bound. It also holds for the empty family. If an accumulating cutting process continued past $4t+\beta-1$ cuts while each finite accumulated family retained the stated hypotheses, that stage would contradict the same bound for the fixed original triangulation. Thus no such process continues indefinitely. The proof retains the original countable-choice and smooth-compatible triangulation scope; it does not postulate an arbitrary unrelated TOP marking.

Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that

itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\operatorname{int}(D)\cap F=\varnothing$ and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha=D\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\beta=D\cap\partial M$, and $\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\cup\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

Assume full AC. Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be a solid torus. Every connected, two-sided, properly embedded incompressible and boundary-incompressible surface $F\subset V$ with nonempty boundary is a disk, either a meridian disk or a boundary-parallel disk. In particular, if $F$ is not boundary-parallel, it is a meridian disk. Any two smooth meridian disks with the same boundary admit a smooth isotopy of embeddings relative to that boundary, with a boundary-fixing topological ambient extension. If both disks are neat, this can be a smooth ambient isotopy relative to the boundary. In addition, every two-sided embedded torus $T\subset\operatorname{int}V$ has a compressing disk in $V$.

Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold, let $F$ be a compact connected smooth subsurface of $\partial M$, and let $N\lhd\pi_1(F)$ be normal. If a continuous disk map into $M$ has its boundary in $\operatorname{Int}F$ with class outside $N$, there is a smoothly properly embedded disk in $M$ whose boundary lies in $\operatorname{Int}F$ and has class outside $N$. No pointwise preservation of the original boundary loop is asserted.

Consequently a compact neatly properly embedded two-sided smooth surface $S$ in such a compact orientable smooth three-manifold is incompressible if and only if its inclusion induces an injection on fundamental groups, component by component. Here incompressibility means absence of a smooth embedded compressing disk, with the conventions of the indicated definition.

Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible $3$-manifold whose boundary components are tori. Let $S\subset M$ be a connected, two-sided, properly embedded incompressible surface with nonempty boundary contained in $\partial M$. Then either $S$ is boundary-incompressible, or $S$ is an annulus boundary-parallel into $\partial M$.

An essential smooth embedded circle in the standard torus $T=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ represents a nonzero primitive integral homology class. A finite disjoint family of essential smooth circles can be carried by a jointly smooth ambient isotopy of $T$ to parallel affine circles. Two essential circles with the same primitive unoriented class are smoothly ambient isotopic. The components between disjoint essential circles have smooth annulus parameters, with prescribed product collars on their boundary circles. No choice axiom is assumed.

Likewise two smooth spanning arcs of a parametrized annulus with the same endpoints and relative winding number are smoothly ambient isotopic relative to any collars on which they already agree. When disjoint, they have a smooth disk-strip parameter; disjoint essential circles in a parametrized annulus have smooth annulus-strip parameters. All isotopies may be stationary near their time endpoints.

Let $Q$ be the smooth Klein bottle with coordinates $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$ modulo $(x,y)\sim(x,y+1)$ and $(x,y)\sim(x+1,-y)$, with its circle-bundle fibers the images of $x=\text{constant}$. Every finite disjoint family of essential two-sided smooth embedded circles can be carried by a jointly smooth ambient isotopy to a family either of vertical fiber circles or of horizontal circles transverse to those fibers. No choice axiom is assumed. The horizontal circles have representatives $y=c$ together with their deck partners $y=-c$, with $c\not\equiv0,1/2$ modulo one. The isotopy may be stationary near its time endpoints.

Assume full AC. All isotopies below are jointly smooth ambient isotopies, stationary near their time endpoints. In this lemma a **neatly proper** surface meets the ambient boundary exactly in its own boundary and transversely there; this is the transverse proper-embedding convention of Hatcher, printed p.3. A boundary-preimage condition alone is insufficient. The explicit common-collar alternative in (a) also covers tangent boundary collars.

(a) In a parametrized smooth ball or solid torus $U$, let two finite disjoint systems of smooth disks meet $\partial U$ exactly in their boundaries, paired so corresponding disks have the same boundary. Suppose either both systems are neatly proper, or the paired systems already agree on supplied embedded boundary collars. Then they are ambient isotopic relative to $\partial U$. In the common-collar alternative the collars may be tangent to $\partial U$, and the isotopy fixes one smaller common collar. The families may be empty.

(b) In the product solid torus $V=D^2\times S^1$, a finite disjoint system of neatly proper incompressible smooth annuli whose boundary circles are vertical product fibers is ambient isotopic, relative to the boundary, to vertical annuli $a_j\times S^1$, with disjoint neatly proper arcs $a_j\subset D^2$. If the annuli are already vertical on a boundary collar, a smaller collar may be fixed.

(c) A finite disjoint system of neatly proper smooth disks in $V$ whose boundary circles are horizontal and meridional is ambient isotopic, relative to the boundary, to horizontal disks (graphs of smooth maps $D^2\to S^1$). The same common-collar assertion holds if the disks are already horizontal there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F$ be a compact smooth surface with boundary, let $M$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$ be a closed embedded smooth surface. If $i:F\to M$ is a smooth embedding whose boundary restriction $i|_{\partial F}$ is transverse to $S$, then there is a smooth isotopy $i_t:F\to M$ through embeddings, fixed on a neighbourhood of $\partial F$, such that $i_1(F)$ is transverse to $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Let $P$ be a compact smooth $k$-manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a Hausdorff smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, and let $f:P\times[0,1]\to N$ be jointly smooth with every $f_t$ a smooth embedding. Suppose the family is stationary on neighborhoods of both time endpoints. For every open neighborhood $W$ of its compact track $f(P\times[0,1])$, there is a jointly smooth isotopy $H_t:N\to N$ of diffeomorphisms with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$ and $H_t\circ f_0=f_t$, supported in a fixed compact subset of $W$ and stationary near its time endpoints. No choice axiom is assumed. The empty source and zero-dimensional source are allowed.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and
the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is
dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second
countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$
and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner
points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be
compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.
Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of
closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation
$f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its
differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the
tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise
preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite
union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same
relative conclusion applies to a fixed corner-adapted triangulated closed neighbourhood piece
whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is
performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary
incompatible boundary data is asserted.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth three-manifold, possibly nonorientable and with boundary, and let $f:F\to M$ be a smooth embedding of a compact smooth surface with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$. Transversality to $\partial M$ is not assumed. Given an open neighborhood $U$ of $C=f(\partial F)$, there is a jointly smooth map $(x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)$ such that each $f_t$ is an embedding, $f_0=f$, every $f_t$ agrees with $f$ on $\partial F$ and outside $f^{-1}(U)$, and $f_t$ is neatly proper for every $t>0$. Time may instead be reparametrized to be stationary near both endpoints; in that version neatness holds after the initial stationary interval.

There is also a jointly continuous ambient isotopy of homeomorphisms $H_t:M\to M$, starting at the identity, supported in $U$, fixing $\partial M$ pointwise, and satisfying $H_t f=f_t$. The construction makes $H_t$ jointly smooth on $(M\setminus C)\times[0,1]$. If $f$ is already neat, the same $f_t$ alternatively admits a jointly smooth ambient extension fixing $\partial M$. No smooth ambient extension at an original tangency is asserted.

Let $F_0=f(F)$ be a compact two-sided smoothly embedded surface in a compact smooth three-manifold, with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$, and let $F_1,H_1$ be its angular neatification from [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]]. The ambient manifold may be nonorientable. If $F_1$ has a smooth compressing disk or smooth boundary-compressing disk, then $F_0$ has a disk of the same type. Boundary-compressing disks can also be transported in the opposite direction: if $F_0$ has one, then $F_1$ has one. Consequently absence of either kind of smooth disk passes from $F_0$ to $F_1$.

Here the boundary-compressing witness has one boundary arc in the surface and the other in $\partial M$, its interior missing both. The construction allows the broader convention of ordinary smooth disk embeddings with tangential endpoint contact, and also gives smooth corner-disk witnesses with transverse surface arcs when that convention is used. No smooth ambient removal of an original surface tangency is asserted.

derivations.claim: For the broader variant first use [F9] to neatify the surface, retaining the disk obstructions and essentiality. Apply the following proof to that neat surface. Concatenate its smooth ambient isotopy with the preliminary smooth embedding isotopy, using stationary time changes at the join; this gives a jointly smooth embedding isotopy. The explicit topological ambient extension of the preliminary path followed by the smooth ambient path supplies the asserted topological ambient alternative. For the main neat-input conclusion no preliminary path is used. On every boundary component the fibration is an ordinary circle bundle over a circle. It has a fiber-preserving smooth identification with a product torus or the standard circle-bundle Klein bottle. To construct it, choose horizontal lifts of the base coordinate in finitely many bundle charts, combine them with a finite bump sum and transport once around the base using [F7]. This gives a circle return diffeomorphism $g$. An increasing angular lift of $g$ is smoothly interpolated to the identity lift when its degree is $+1$; a decreasing lift is smoothly interpolated to $\theta\mapsto-\theta$ when its degree is $-1$. Their derivatives retain their sign. Using this path on a base interval, stationary in endpoint collars, identifies the mapping torus with the product or reflection mapping torus, respectively. Every component of $\partial F$ is essential on its boundary component: an innermost boundary disk would compress $F$, since an annulus or torus is not a disk. Its normal line in $\partial M$ is the restriction of the two-sided normal of $F$, so in the Klein-bottle case it is two-sided. Apply [F4] to make these circles vertical or horizontal in each boundary component, extending the boundary isotopies into collars by [F7]. No orientability of $M$ is used.

Choose fiber cores $C_i$ containing all exceptional fibers, and choose one regular fiber if that list was empty. Put $F$ transverse to these finitely many curves. Here is the needed codimension-two use of [F6]: choose finitely many supported coordinate vector fields spanning the target tangent spaces near the compact core set; their short flows give a finite parameter family of ambient diffeomorphisms whose evaluation on $F$ is a submersion near every possible core intersection. Away from that neighborhood there are none. Parametric transversality gives a sufficiently small parameter with transverse slice. The path of parameters gives an ambient isotopy, fixed near $\partial M$. Thus there are finitely many intersection points. In each fibered core neighborhood, transversality makes $F$ a finite collection of disk graphs over the meridian plane. Shrink the neighborhood until all these graphs are transverse to the fiber direction, and straighten them to constant core-coordinate meridian disks by graph interpolation. On the finite ordered core coordinates the disks remain disjoint on this small neighborhood; extend in a larger collar by [F7]. All other parts of $F$ are separated from the core neighborhoods by compactness. Consequently $F$ meets each selected small fibered solid torus $N_i$ in horizontal meridian disks, each meeting its core once.

Remove the interiors of $N_i$, obtaining a circle bundle $M_0\to B_0$ over a connected compact surface with boundary. Choose finitely many disjoint proper base arcs cutting $B_0$ to one disk, and let $A_j$ be their inverse-image annuli. Cutting $M_0$ along them gives a product solid torus $W=D^2\times S^1$. The finite base cut can be read from a triangulation [F8]: a dual spanning tree first joins its triangles to one polygon, and finitely many polygon side arcs remove its handles and extra boundary components. Choose among all such transverse configurations, with horizontal core disks, normalized outer boundary collars and the displayed base-arc cut, one minimizing lexicographically the number of core intersections and then the number of intersection components with the annuli $A_j$. Only finite integer minima are selected. The neighborhoods and their base-arc end collars may be shrunk again after an isotopy; such a shrink preserves the displayed disk graphs and only appends their already transverse graph strips to the annulus ends, so it creates no new intersection component. Put $F$ transverse to the annuli by [F6]. A circle innermost in an $A_j$ bounds a disk there. It cannot be essential on $F$. Its disk on $F$ and the annulus disk bound a ball by irreducibility. The remainder of $F$ lies outside that ball: for a proper annulus it reaches $\partial M$; for a closed torus, lying inside would put the whole torus in the closed ball. Shrink that parametrized ball a little by [F7] to move the torus into its interior; [F2] then gives a compression, pulled back by the isotopy. The marked disk push from [F2] removes the circle and any further intersections inside the disk on $F$. Its final disk is near the annulus disk and misses all cores, so it decreases the first count or retains it and decreases the second. This contradicts minimality. Thus no circle of $F\cap A_j$ is inessential in $A_j$.

An outermost returning arc in an $A_j$ cuts off a disk $D$ with its other edge $\beta$ on a fiber circle of $\partial M_0$. Its interior misses $F$. If its endpoints are on an original boundary component of $M$, essentiality of its edge on $F$ would make it a boundary compression. If that edge is inessential, its ends lie on one boundary circle of $F$. This is also impossible: $D$ lies on one coherent normal side of the two-sided $F$, whereas a fiber interval between successive crossings of one affine horizontal boundary circle approaches opposite sides at its two ends. The same normal-side argument applies on a Klein bottle in its orientation double cover; the boundary lift is horizontal there. If instead $\beta$ lies on $\partial N_i$, it joins two different meridian disks of $F\cap N_i$ by that same argument. In the constant core coordinates of step 2.1, successive crossings along the regular boundary fiber project to successive core-coordinate values. The projected interval has length less than one core period and contains no other intersection with $F$. Its radial ruling in $N_i$ is therefore an embedded strip: the core coordinate is strictly monotone on it, so even an exceptional fiber's meridional winding creates no self-intersection. Join this strip to $D$. This is an embedded bigon between $F$ and a core interval, with interior missing both. The smooth graph bigon move across it cancels the two core intersections, contrary to the first minimum. We have proved that every arc of $F\cap A_j$ spans its annulus. By [F4], straighten these arcs to graphs over the base interval, and straighten the essential circles to fibers. Circles and spanning arcs cannot coexist in one annulus. Extend these moves through small product neighborhoods, retaining the normalized boundary collars. Along spanning arcs the two transverse surface planes force $F$ to be transverse to the fiber; along fiber circles straighten its other tangent to a base direction. Thus near the cut annuli and the outer boundary, $F$ is already horizontal or vertical as appropriate.

Let $F_1$ be the surface cut open in $W$. It is incompressible there. Indeed a compressing disk has boundary bounding a disk $D'$ on $F$, by incompressibility in $M$. If $D'$ were contained in $F_1$, it would not be a compression. Otherwise it crosses a cut annulus or a deleted core disk. Its union with the compressing disk bounds a ball by irreducibility. As in step 3.1, the rest of $F$ lies outside; the alternative of a torus inside the ball would itself supply a compression. The smooth disk push replaces $D'$ by a disk in $W$, reducing core intersections or retaining them and reducing annulus intersections. This contradicts the chosen minimum. Every boundary circle of $F_1$ is vertical or horizontal on $\partial W$: the collar models of step 4.1 are already vertical or transverse to the fiber, and their graph parameters agree across the rounded base-disk corners. Such a circle is essential on this torus; in the horizontal case its projection is a local diffeomorphism onto the base boundary circle, so has nonzero degree.

Apply [F3] to each component with boundary in the orientable solid torus $W$, then [F2] to a boundary-incompressible component. The alternatives are a meridian disk or a boundary-parallel annulus; a boundary-parallel disk is excluded by the essential boundary circles. Closed torus components are excluded by [F2]. Suppose a boundary-parallel annulus has horizontal boundary. Its parallel boundary annulus contains an interval of a vertical fiber over an original boundary segment of the cut base disk, away from the cut-arc faces. Its product gives a boundary-compressing disk whose boundary edge is that vertical interval. This disk can be made to miss all other components: remove intersection circles using incompressibility of $F_1$ and disk replacement; an edgemost remaining arc nearest that interval cuts off a disk with interior missing $F_1$. Its vertical boundary edge lies on one component of $\partial M_0$. The exact argument of step 4.1 now gives either a forbidden boundary compression or a cancellation of two core intersections. Thus horizontal-boundary parallel annuli do not occur. The remaining annuli have vertical boundary. A disk cannot have vertical boundary, since a product fiber generates $\pi_1(W)$ and does not bound a disk there. Thus the remaining disks have horizontal boundary.

A vertical circle on $\partial W$ and a horizontal circle have nonzero algebraic intersection, equal up to sign to the latter's nonzero base degree. Disjoint boundary circles cannot have both types. Thus $F_1$ consists entirely of vertical-boundary annuli or entirely of horizontal-boundary disks. In the first case apply [F5](b), and in the second apply [F5](c). All boundary and cut-face collars were already of the corresponding type, so choose the target product/graph systems to agree on smaller collars and retain them in the simultaneous isotopies. The maps then reglue smoothly across each cut annulus and agree with the identity in the deleted core neighborhoods. The vertical case has no core disks, since their boundary would be horizontal; it yields a union of regular fibers. In the horizontal case those unchanged core disks are already transverse to every fiber in $N_i$, so the reglued whole surface is horizontal. Every step used an actual smooth ambient isotopy; stationary time changes at the finite joins give joint smoothness, including the parameter endpoints. This proves the alternative in the original ambient category, also when $M$ is nonorientable.

For a horizontal $F$, its proper local projection off the exceptional points is a finite cover, with constant positive sheet count $n$ since the base is connected. In the fibered solid-torus model a transverse meridian disk projects to a disk by the order-$q_i$ branched map; hence there are $n/q_i$ preimages over the $i$th exceptional point. Triangulate the underlying base by [F8], including those finitely many marked points by a local subdivision, and lift it. Every ordinary cell has $n$ lifts; only the marked vertices have $n/q_i$ rather than $n$ lifts. The finite alternating count gives $$\chi(F)=n\chi(B)-\sum_i(n-n/q_i),$$ as claimed. Finally cut the fibers at their intersections with $F$. Over an ordinary chart the resulting segments form product interval charts. Near an exceptional fiber use its finite cyclic model: the action permutes the lifted cut segments freely, so the quotient of each segment chart is again a disk times an interval, not an orbifold interval chart. These charts paste along whole segment fibers, possibly reversing their interval coordinate, and supply an interval bundle on the cut-open manifold. Two-sidedness provides its two boundary copies of $F$. No orientability assumption on $M$ is needed for this interval-bundle conclusion.

The components between disjoint essential circles have smooth annulus parameters, with prescribed product collars on their boundary circles. No choice axiom is assumed.

Likewise two smooth spanning arcs of a parametrized annulus with the same endpoints and relative winding number are smoothly ambient isotopic relative to any collars on which they already agree. When disjoint, they have a smooth disk-strip parameter; disjoint essential circles in a parametrized annulus have smooth annulus-strip parameters. All isotopies may be stationary near their time endpoints.

The bounded region of a smooth embedded
circle in the oriented plane, together with its boundary, is a smooth manifold
with boundary diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Let $D_0,D_1$ be two
such closed regions. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary
diffeomorphism $b:\partial D_0\to\partial D_1$ extends to an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $B:D_0\to D_1$. More precisely, for
specified smooth inward collars $c_i:\partial D_i\times[0,\epsilon)\to D_i$
with $c_i(p,0)=p$, the extension may be required to satisfy
$B(c_0(p,r))=c_1(b(p),r)$ for every sufficiently small $r\ge0$. In addition, given interior points $p_i\in D_i$ and an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $q$ from a neighborhood of $p_0$ onto a neighborhood of $p_1$, the extension can agree with $q$ near $p_0$ while retaining the prescribed boundary collars.

Let $P$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a boundaryless Hausdorff smooth manifold, and let $i:P\to N$ be a smooth embedding. Let $Z\subset N$ be a closed embedded smooth submanifold without boundary. If $i$ is transverse to $Z$ along $\partial P$, then an arbitrarily small jointly smooth ambient isotopy, supported in any prescribed neighborhood of $i(P)$ and fixed on a neighborhood of $i(\partial P)$, makes $i(P)$ transverse to $Z$. The isotopy may be stationary near its time endpoints. No choice axiom is assumed. The same assertion holds for any finite family of such $Z$, provided the initial boundary restriction is transverse to every member. Empty source and empty intersection are allowed.

For a parametrized smooth $n$-ball $B$ and a parametrized smooth boundary $(n-1)$-disk $W$, the pair $(B,W)$ is diffeomorphic to the standard ball with a hemispherical window. The diffeomorphism can retain the specified window parameter, using stereographic parameters on the standard hemisphere and allowing the necessary orientation of that parameter. No choice axiom is assumed.

Consequently, attaching a parametrized smooth $n$-ball to a smooth $n$-manifold along such a window does not change its diffeomorphism type, provided an attaching collar and corner rounding are supplied. Two smooth circle-bundle fibrations of the same torus with equal unoriented primitive fiber class are carried to one another by a jointly smooth isotopy of the torus starting at the identity and stationary near its time endpoints.

Their union is then a smooth Seifert fibration of the glued manifold. The two boundary tori may belong to the same piece. In that case every component of the smooth cut-open manifold $X\mathbin{\|}S$ is injective on fundamental groups into $X$. No irreducibility or choice assumption is required.

This is an interface for a supplied smooth product. It asserts neither triangulability of an arbitrary topological three-manifold nor smoothing of an arbitrary ambient PL marking.

Let $P$ be a compact smooth $k$-manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a Hausdorff smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, and let $f:P\times[0,1]\to N$ be jointly smooth with every $f_t$ a smooth embedding. Suppose the family is stationary on neighborhoods of both time endpoints. For every open neighborhood $W$ of its compact track $f(P\times[0,1])$, there is a jointly smooth isotopy $H_t:N\to N$ of diffeomorphisms with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$ and $H_t\circ f_0=f_t$, supported in a fixed compact subset of $W$ and stationary near its time endpoints. $$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Given an open neighborhood $U$ of $C=f(\partial F)$, there is a jointly smooth map $(x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)$ such that each $f_t$ is an embedding, $f_0=f$, every $f_t$ agrees with $f$ on $\partial F$ and outside $f^{-1}(U)$, and $f_t$ is neatly proper for every $t>0$. derivations.claim: First apply [F9] to the given surface, fixed pointwise on its boundary. The resulting surface is neat. Incompressibility passes to it, and a boundary-compressing witness passes in either direction; absence of boundary compressions therefore passes as well. Work with this neat representative for the following smooth collar constructions. The boundary-fixing topological ambient extension pulls any resulting boundary-parallel product back to the actual original surface. Thus this preparation does not add a neatness hypothesis to the Statement. Take a small product neighborhood of $A$ and collars of its incident boundary tori. They exist by a finite coordinate construction: choose the normal side using orientations of $M$ and $A$, combine finitely many adapted chart fields by normalized finite bumps, and use their short flow and the local inverse and compact separation arguments in [F7]. Normalize the two boundary curves on each incident torus by [F3]. Their parallel strip parameters and the product parameter of $A$ supply circle coordinates on the neighborhood, agreeing at the attaching rims. Circle parameter discrepancies have degree $\pm1$ and are adjusted by interpolation of their increasing, or decreasing, angular lifts; this is finite. Round the quadrant corners in the base coordinate, keeping the circle coordinate. The resulting neighborhood $N_0$ is an ordinary circle bundle with $A$ vertical. If the annulus meets two different original tori, its base is a pair of pants with two original boundary circles and one internal boundary. If it meets one original torus, its band attaches to the same base boundary circle: the two possible band identifications give a pair of pants with two internal boundaries, or a once-punctured Möbius band with one. The total space is orientable, since it is a submanifold of $M$; in the Möbius case the fiber orientation reverses with the base orientation. These are actual finite band-and-collar quotient parameters. The internal frontier consists of at most two tori.

We first fill compressible frontier tori, before addressing boundary-parallel ones. For $N_0$, frontier groups inject into its group by [F2]. Use this injection for the initial iteration. After the only possible intermediate filling, its explicit group calculation below will verify the invariant before another iteration. If a frontier torus is compressible in $M$, choose a compressing disk and put it transverse to the other frontiers by [F3]. Its intersection consists of finitely many circles. Remove any inessential circle on a frontier by an innermost disk replacement: choose its frontier disk with interior disjoint from the compressing disk, replace the latter's subdisk by it and push slightly to the side of the retained disk. The disk parameters in [F3] and quadrant rounding give an embedded smooth disk with the same essential original boundary and fewer intersections. If a remaining intersection is essential on its frontier, an innermost circle on the disk cuts off a compressing disk whose interior misses the entire frontier. If no intersection remains, the original disk already has this property. Thus some frontier $T$ has a clean compressing disk $D$. It cannot lie in $N$, since its boundary class is nonzero on $T$ and $\pi_1(T)\to\pi_1(N)$ is injective. The connected disk interior consequently lies on the exterior side of $N$.

The connected $N$ lies outside that ball: it misses the compressed sphere and contains an original boundary torus of $M$, whereas $B$ is an interior ball. The disk neighborhood restored by reversing compression is also on this non-ball side, because its rim strip is joined to $N$ through the gap removed from $T$. Hence reversal attaches a marked $1$-handle to $B$; it does not remove a possibly knotted handle from its interior. Its two disk windows have the parallel-copy parameters of $D$, and [F4] standardizes them. The result is a solid torus $U$ outside $N$, with boundary exactly $T$. It contains no other frontier, since $B$ and the small disk neighborhood miss $N$ except at $T$. Thus this filling extends the actual Seifert structure, leaves $A$ vertical and caps that base boundary by a disk with cone order $b$ (regular if $b=1$).

There are initially at most two frontiers. The only filling that can leave another frontier is the pair-of-pants case with just one original boundary torus; its new base is an annulus with at most one cone. Its remaining boundary groups still inject, by this explicit finite calculation. Before filling the orientable circle bundle over a pair of pants has group $F(a,c)\times\langle h\rangle$: lift the two free base generators, and the oriented fiber $h$ is central and injective by [F2]. Filling adds the primitive relation $c^q h^p=1$, with $q\ge1$, by [F2]'s gluing pushout. The quotient by central $h$ is $\mathbb Z*C_q$. The two boundary base loops have images $a$ and $(ac)^{-1}$, both of infinite order by reduced words (for $q=1$, both are $a^{\pm1}$). Also $h$ has infinite order: the presentation maps to the additive reals by $h\mapsto1$, $c\mapsto-p/q$, $a\mapsto0$. Thus a boundary element projecting trivially must first have zero base exponent, then zero fiber exponent. This proves boundary-torus injection after the intermediate filling. Step 2.1 is therefore applicable again. After finitely many such steps, either no frontier remains or every remaining frontier is incompressible in $M$.

If $P$ is on the exterior side of $N$, it is exactly the adjacent exterior component, so absorb it into $N$, extending the fibration as a product by [F5]. Suppose instead that $N$ lies on the $P$ side. It is then contained in $P$, since the latter occupies that whole component between $T$ and the original boundary. The product contains only one original boundary torus of $M$. Thus this is impossible if $N$ already contains two original boundary tori. If $N$ still has two frontiers, it is the original pair-of-pants bundle with one original boundary; the other frontier $T'$ is an incompressible smooth torus in $P$. By [F6], every cut piece of $P$ along $T'$ injects into $\pi_1(P)$. The connected $N$ is one such piece, since its only interior boundary in $P$ is $T'$. But $\pi_1(N)$ surjects onto the nonabelian free rank-two base group [F2], while $\pi_1(P)=\mathbb Z^2$ is abelian. This is a contradiction. This argument treats $N$ as a possible proper submanifold of the collar; it does not incorrectly infer that nonabelian $N$ cannot sit inside a product without an injection proof.

It remains to exclude the $N$-side collar when there is one frontier and one original boundary. In that case $N=P$, since it has exactly the two boundary tori of $P$ and no interior frontier in it. A fixed point of the initial fiber gives a section disk. Its boundary consists of an essential spanning arc of $A$ and an arc in the original boundary torus. This is a forbidden boundary compression of $A$. Thus the collar can never be on the $N$ side. Every remaining frontier is therefore an exterior product collar and can be absorbed.

Each solid-torus filling or collar absorption removes a frontier, and initially there were at most two. At the end $N$ has no internal frontier; it is nonempty, closed and relatively open in connected $M$, hence equals $M$. Its fibration is the smooth Seifert structure constructed in steps 4.1 and 6.1. The neat representative of the annulus was retained throughout. The conclusion is a smooth Seifert structure on the unchanged ambient manifold, so it proves the original choice-free Statement without asserting that an original tangential annulus is smoothly ambient isotopic to a vertical one. The only product-group comparison used the explicit flat-product compression and cut-injection bridge [F6]; no arbitrary smooth/PL compatibility or general topological triangulation assertion entered. All choices and modifications were finite.
